From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, May 22, 2025 at 9:14 AM PDT
Subject: Approval request: Private release gating checklist for upgrade + rollback (Beta/GA readiness)

Sean,

Requesting SRE leadership approval on the proposed release gating checklist for Redwood Private upgrades/rollbacks before we cut the Beta train and then GA.

This is intended to be the default “stop the line” gate for Private releases that include upgrade tooling and/or migration-affecting changes.

What I need from you:
- Approve the checklist + minimum evidence required to pass gates
- Confirm who is the named SRE approver for Beta and GA cuts (you vs. Rafael)
- Confirm whether we require a rollback drill in staging as a hard gate for GA (proposed: yes)

Proposed gating checklist (high-level)
1) Upgrade path is supported by compatibility policy (N-1 -> N is hard requirement)
2) Preflight checks present + enforced for: cluster health, storage headroom, DB connectivity, RBAC/OIDC reachability, TLS/DNS, artifact availability
3) Backup succeeds prior to any irreversible step; backup artifacts are encrypted and verifiable
4) Rollback entry points exist + are deterministic; idempotency verified
5) Control-plane / data-plane sequencing is enforced (CP complete + ready before DP rollout)
6) Observability: dashboards and audit events for start/stop, precheck pass/fail, backup complete, rollback invoked
7) Test evidence: CI matrix green + at least 1 full in-place upgrade run + 1 rollback run on ephemeral cluster

Evidence attached:
- Private-Release-Gating-Checklist-v1.3.pdf
- upgrade-e2e-matrix-2025-05-21.csv
- nightly-upgrade-e2e-run-2025-05-21.txt

Key references:
- Change management policy draft (Confluence): /policies-and-process/change-management/private-release-gating-and-change-management
- CI matrix (Confluence): /eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/private-installer-integration-test-matrix
- Recent incidents/tickets motivating gates: SUP-18421 (DB migration fail), SUP-18577 (storage headroom)

Delta vs last train:
- Hard-block precheck on storage headroom (warn-only previously)
- Rollback command now consumes stored upgrade state (reduces “manual archaeology”)
- Audit log events emitted for enterprise traceability (requested by multiple customers)

If you’re good with it, please reply with “Approved for Beta” and any conditions. I’ll incorporate and route to Vivek/Talia for the program checklist.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O’Brien
Release Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, May 22, 2025 at 10:03 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Approval request: Private release gating checklist for upgrade + rollback (Beta/GA readiness)

Connor,

This is directionally right. Before I approve, I need a couple clarifications:

1) What is the “minimum green” for CI? I don’t want GA blocked by a flaky scenario, but I also don’t want us waving through without coverage.

2) For backups: are we requiring both snapshot + logical dump, or allowing either depending on backend? (On-prem constraints have bitten us.)

3) For DB migrations: do we have guardrails to prevent long locks? SUP-18421 was basically “migration ran and wedged the app.”

4) For rollback: are we guaranteeing rollback across a migration that already ran? If not, we need explicit language in the checklist and in the operator runbook.

Reply with proposed answers + what we’re actually enforcing in tooling vs. process.

- Sean


---

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, May 22, 2025 at 11:12 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Approval request: Private release gating checklist for upgrade + rollback (Beta/GA readiness)

All good questions — proposed enforcement below.

1) CI “minimum green”
- Beta gate: 1x N-1 -> N upgrade E2E on ephemeral cluster + precheck suite must be green; allow one quarantined scenario if it’s tagged as flaky with an open owner issue.
- GA gate: 2x independent E2E upgrade runs (different cluster/storage profiles) + 1 rollback run; zero quarantines on upgrade/rollback paths.

Sahana can confirm current signal:
- Nightly run 2025-05-21: PASS (upgrade) and PASS (rollback) on k8s 1.29 + CSI snapshot backend (see attached txt)
- k8s 1.28 + EBS snapshot path: PASS for upgrade, rollback PASS but duration is high (not failing)

2) Backup requirement (enforced by installer)
- We require “at least one restorable backup mechanism” before any irreversible step.
- Backend-specific:
  - Cloud/VPC: CSI/EBS snapshots are default; logical DB dump optional.
  - On-prem/air-gapped: logical DB dump is supported; snapshot hook is optional depending on storage class.

The installer orchestration (PR #4850) enforces “backup step succeeded” and records backup metadata in upgrade state. We’re not requiring both snapshot+logical as a hard gate.

3) DB migration guardrails
- We have guardrails landing in core (redwood PR #29210): lock timeouts + idempotency checks + safe defaults.
- Enforcement today:
  - Pre-upgrade plan includes a “migration risk” flag when there are non-trivial migrations; surfaces operator guidance.
  - GA gate includes “migration duration < threshold in staging” evidence (SRE owned threshold; we proposed 10 min P95 in staging).

4) Rollback guarantees
- We are NOT guaranteeing rollback across all schema migrations once applied.
- What we are guaranteeing:
  - Rollback entry points are deterministic for control-plane + chart state.
  - For DB: rollback is supported only when migrations are backward-compatible or when a restore-from-backup is used.

We will make this explicit:
- Checklist language: “Rollback requires restore if non-reversible migration applied”
- Operator runbook: decision tree (rollback vs. restore vs. manual intervention)

Tooling vs. process:
- Tooling hard blocks: unsupported upgrade paths (compat policy), failing prechecks (blockers), backup not completed, artifact verification failure.
- Process gates: approval sign-off, comms template, maintenance window confirmation.

If you want, I can add a bold “Rollback semantics” section to the checklist front page so this doesn’t get misconstrued.

Connor

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Sahana Iyer <sahana.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, May 22, 2025 at 1:47 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Approval request: Private release gating checklist for upgrade + rollback (Beta/GA readiness)

+1 to making rollback semantics explicit on page 1.

Two conditions I want captured for GA:
- A staged “rollback drill” in a clean environment where we intentionally fail mid-upgrade (e.g., kill the migration job / block control-plane readiness) and verify the operator can recover using rollback/restore guidance.
- Upgrade window annotation: release train should include a standard way to tag upgrade windows so alerts are attributable (helps on-call and postmortems).

Assuming those are in the checklist, I’m comfortable with SRE approving Beta based on current evidence.

Rafael
SRE (On-call & Reliability Execution)

Subject: Re: Approval request: Private release gating checklist for upgrade + rollback (Beta/GA readiness)

Approved for Beta with the following conditions:

1) Checklist must state clearly:
- rollback semantics for DB (restore required where migrations aren’t reversible)
- what is hard-blocked by tooling vs. what is a human gate

2) For GA, Rafael’s two conditions are required hard gates:
- rollback drill with failure injection (mid-upgrade) + documented operator recovery
- upgrade window annotation method agreed with SRE (so alerts/dashboards aren’t noisy and we can correlate)

Approver: For Beta cuts, Rafael can sign off day-to-day; I’ll remain escalation approver and final sign-off for GA readiness.

Once you revise the checklist PDF, send the updated version and I’ll add a brief note in the SRE runbook that this is the standard gate.

- Sean
Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead
Redwood Inference
